title: Mature B-Cell Neoplasms by Flow Cytometry: CLL, Mantle Cell, Follicular and Hairy Cell
summary: Use light-chain restriction and marker patterns to separate CLL from mantle cell lymphoma, follicular lymphoma and hairy cell leukemia, and apply the 5,000/µL rule that separates CLL from MBL.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 34 Hits 8 and 10 and Trap 2, with mantle cell and follicular lymphoma as comparisons. Checked against Hallek 2025, Gajzer & Fromm 2025, Shah 2026 and Laganà 2025. Not taught: del17p prognosis (Hit 8), purine-analog therapy (Hit 10), Burkitt and B-ALL details (Hit 9, Trap 6), bcl-6 in follicular lymphoma — not checked. Hit 8 omits the ≥ 3-month duration and the marrow-cytopenia exception, both taught here.

objectives: Explain light-chain restriction as evidence of a B-cell clone.
Distinguish CLL, mantle cell, follicular and hairy cell phenotypes.
Apply the CLL vs MBL count and duration criteria.

scenes.title: Two CD5-positive clones
scenes.altText: Two invented flow reports, both monotypic (κ-restricted) CD19+ B cells that are CD5+. Patient 1: 12 × 10⁹/L clonal B cells for 4 months; CD23+, CD20 dim, surface Ig dim, FMC7−, CD200+. Patient 2: CD23−, CD20 bright, FMC7+, CD200−. Question token: “Same CD5 — same disease?”

cues.text: Two patients have clonal B cells that carry CD5. Patient one: 12 billion per litre for four months, CD23 positive, dim CD20 and dim surface immunoglobulin, FMC7 negative.
Patient two: CD23 negative, bright CD20, FMC7 positive and CD200 negative.
They share CD5. Do they share a diagnosis?

scenes.title: Clonality first
scenes.altText: Clonality card: a mature B-cell neoplasm is a clone — all cells express only kappa or only lambda light chain (monotypic surface light chain), unlike the mixed κ and λ of normal B cells. Panel card (Laganà 2025): pan-B markers CD19, CD20, CD22, cyCD79a, plus CD5, CD10, CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD79b, CD103, CD25, CD123, CD43, CD38, sIg κ/λ. Token: intensity (dim vs bright) matters as much as positive vs negative.

cues.text: Normal B cells are a mix: some use kappa light chains, some lambda. A B-cell neoplasm is a single clone, so all its cells show only one light chain. That is light-chain restriction.
A lymphoproliferative panel adds pan-B markers such as CD19 and CD20 to discriminating markers: CD5, CD10, CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD79b, and hairy-cell markers CD103, CD25 and CD123.
Read intensity, not only positive or negative: dim CD20 and dim surface immunoglobulin are as informative as a missing marker.
Then sort the clone by its pattern.

props.title: Clonality
lines: Normal B: κ and λ mixed

scenes.title: Four patterns
scenes.altText: Four phenotype cards (Gajzer & Fromm 2025; Hallek 2025; Shah 2026). CLL/SLL: CD5+, CD23+, CD200+, CD20 dim, surface light chain dim to absent, CD79b low, FMC7−. Mantle cell lymphoma: CD5+, CD20 normal to bright, FMC7+, CD23−, CD200−; confirm with cyclin D1 or SOX11 by IHC, or t(11;14) by FISH. Follicular lymphoma: CD10+ (~90%), CD5−, CD43−, BCL2 increased; associated with t(14;18). Hairy cell leukemia: increased forward and side scatter, CD20 bright, CD11c+, CD25+, CD103+, CD123+, annexin A1+, CD5− and CD10−; BRAF V600E in 90–95%; TRAP can help on IHC.

cues.text: CLL is CD5 and CD23 positive, CD200 positive, with dim CD20, dim or absent surface light chain, low CD79b, and FMC7 negative. It whispers.
Mantle cell lymphoma is also CD5 positive, but CD23 and CD200 negative, with normal to bright CD20 and FMC7 positive. Confirm it with cyclin D1 or SOX11 staining, or t(11;14) by FISH.
Follicular lymphoma is usually CD10 positive and CD5 negative, with increased BCL2, and is associated with t(14;18).
Hairy cell leukemia shows large cells on scatter, bright CD20, and CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123, without CD5 or CD10. About 90 to 95 percent carry BRAF V600E.

scenes.title: Counting to CLL
scenes.altText: CLL criteria card (Hallek 2025): ≥ 5,000 clonal B lymphocytes/µL in peripheral blood for at least 3 months, clonality confirmed by flow cytometry; fewer than 5,000/µL without lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, cytopenias or symptoms = monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL); cytopenia caused by a typical marrow infiltrate = CLL regardless of count. Back to the hook: Patient 1 = 12,000/µL for 4 months, CLL phenotype → CLL. Patient 2 = CD5+ but CD23−, CD20 bright, FMC7+, CD200− → suspect mantle cell lymphoma; confirm cyclin D1/SOX11 or t(11;14).

cues.text: CLL needs at least 5,000 clonal B lymphocytes per microlitre of blood for at least three months, with clonality confirmed by flow cytometry.
Fewer than 5,000, with no enlarged nodes or organs, cytopenias or symptoms, is monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis.
But cytopenia caused by a typical marrow infiltrate means CLL, whatever the blood count.
Back to the patients: patient one has 12,000 per microlitre for four months with the CLL pattern. That is CLL.
Patient two shares CD5 but has the mantle cell pattern. Confirm with cyclin D1 or SOX11 staining or t(11;14).

props.label: Patient 2 → suspect MCL: cyclin D1 / t(11;14)

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “CD5+ B cells = CLL” (✓ mantle cell is also CD5+ — check CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD20 intensity, cyclin D1); “Any count of clonal CLL-type cells = CLL” (✓ < 5,000/µL without other findings = MBL); “Hairy cell leukemia is CD5+ like CLL” (✓ HCL is CD5− and CD10−, with CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123).

cues.text: Trap one: CD5 positive B cells mean CLL. Mantle cell lymphoma is CD5 positive too; separate them with CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD20 brightness and cyclin D1.
Trap two: any number of CLL-type clonal cells is CLL. Below 5,000 per microlitre with no nodes, organomegaly, cytopenias or symptoms, it is monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis.
Trap three: hairy cell leukemia is CD5 positive like CLL. It is CD5 and CD10 negative, and expresses CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123.

props.title: ✗ “CD5+ B cells = CLL.”
lines: ✓ MCL is CD5+ too: CD23−, FMC7+, cyclin D1

scenes.title: CLL whispers, mantle shouts
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “CLL whispers (dim CD20, dim sIg, FMC7−, CD23+); mantle shouts (bright CD20, FMC7+, CD23−) — both wear CD5.” Plus “Hairy cells wear 4 badges: 11c, 25, 103, 123.” Tokens: Whisper · Shout · 4 badges. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: CLL whispers, mantle shouts, and both wear CD5. CLL is dim, CD23 positive and FMC7 negative; mantle cell is bright, CD23 negative and FMC7 positive. Hairy cells wear four badges: CD11c, 25, 103 and 123.
Where it breaks: atypical phenotypes occur; flow alone does not make the diagnosis; and cyclin D1, SOX11 or t(11;14) confirm mantle cell lymphoma.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “CLL: CD5+ CD23+ CD200+, dim CD20/sIg, FMC7− · ≥ 5,000/µL ≥ 3 months (else MBL)”, “MCL: CD5+ CD23− FMC7+, cyclin D1/t(11;14) · FL: CD10+ BCL2 · HCL: CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, BRAF V600E”.

cues.text: CD5 alone does not mean CLL: CLL is CD23-positive and dim, mantle cell lymphoma is CD23-negative and bright with cyclin D1, and fewer than 5,000 clonal cells per microlitre without other findings is MBL.

props.label: CLL: CD5+ CD23+ CD200+ dim · FMC7− · ≥ 5,000/µL ≥ 3 mo (else MBL)
MCL: CD5+ CD23− FMC7+, cyclin D1 · FL: CD10+ BCL2 · HCL: 11c/25/103/123

explanation.what: Plain language: flow cytometry reads the protein “badges” on blood cells; a cancerous B-cell clone shows one light-chain type and a badge pattern that names the disease. Scientific terms: immunophenotype, light-chain restriction (κ/λ), CD5, CD10, CD20, CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD79b, CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL), cyclin D1, SOX11, t(11;14), t(14;18), BRAF V600E.
explanation.why: A neoplasm arises from one B cell, so its progeny share one light chain and a characteristic antigen profile reflecting the cell of origin. CD5 is shared by CLL and mantle cell lymphoma, so other markers and genetics separate them.
explanation.measure: CLL: CD5, CD19, CD20 (dim), CD23, CD200 +, low sIg/CD79b, FMC7 −; ≥ 5,000/µL clonal B cells ≥ 3 months; < 5,000 without other findings = MBL; marrow-infiltrate cytopenia = CLL (Hallek 2025). MCL: CD5 +, CD20 normal–bright, FMC7 +, CD23 −, CD200 −; cyclin D1/SOX11 IHC or t(11;14) FISH. FL: CD10 + (~90%), CD5 −, CD43 −, BCL2 increased; t(14;18). HCL: high scatter, CD20 bright, CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123 +, CD5 −, CD10 − (Gajzer 2025); annexin A1 +; BRAF V600E 90–95% (Shah 2026).
explanation.differs: CLL vs MCL (both CD5 +: CD23, CD200, FMC7, CD20 intensity, cyclin D1); CLL vs MBL (count, duration, findings); FL (CD10 +) vs HCL (CD103/CD25/CD11c/CD123).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: a CD5+ case to classify, the CLL count threshold, HCL markers, and which test confirms mantle cell lymphoma.

right.label: MBL
points: No nodes, organomegaly, cytopenias or symptoms

mnemonic.text: CLL whispers, mantle shouts — both wear CD5. Hairy cells wear four badges: 11c, 25, 103, 123.
mnemonic.explanation: CLL is dim (CD20, sIg) with CD23 + and FMC7 −; mantle cell is bright with FMC7 + and CD23 −; HCL expresses CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123.
mnemonic.limitation: Atypical phenotypes occur; flow alone is not diagnostic; cyclin D1/SOX11/t(11;14) confirm MCL.

analogyLimitations: Flow reports are invented and simplified.
Marker intensities are shown as words, not plots.
“Whisper/shout” is an analogy for antigen intensity only.
takeaway: CD5 alone does not mean CLL: CLL is CD23-positive and dim, mantle cell lymphoma is CD23-negative and bright with cyclin D1, and fewer than 5,000 clonal cells per microlitre without other findings is MBL.

questions.stem: Clonal κ-restricted B cells are CD5+, CD23−, CD200−, FMC7+, with bright CD20. Which test best confirms the likely diagnosis?

options.text: Cyclin D1 (or SOX11) immunostaining or FISH for t(11;14)
options.rationale: Correct. The pattern suggests mantle cell lymphoma, confirmed by cyclin D1/SOX11 or t(11;14).
Incorrect. BRAF V600E supports hairy cell leukemia, which is CD5−.

options.text: No further testing: CD5+ means CLL
options.rationale: Incorrect. CLL is CD23+, CD200+, FMC7− with dim CD20.
Incorrect. t(14;18) is associated with follicular lymphoma, which is usually CD10+ and CD5−.

questions.stem: An asymptomatic adult has 3,200/µL clonal B cells with a typical CLL phenotype, no lymphadenopathy, organomegaly or cytopenias. What is the diagnosis?

options.rationale: Correct. Fewer than 5,000/µL without other findings defines MBL.
Incorrect. CLL requires ≥ 5,000/µL for ≥ 3 months, or cytopenia from marrow infiltration.
Incorrect. The cells are clonal (light-chain restricted).
Incorrect. The phenotype is typical of CLL, not mantle cell.

questions.stem: Large clonal B cells with high side scatter are CD20 bright, CD11c+, CD25+, CD103+, CD123+, CD5− and CD10−. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.rationale: Correct. CD11c, CD25, CD103 and CD123 without CD5/CD10 is the classic HCL profile.
Incorrect. CLL is CD5+ and CD23+ with dim CD20.
Incorrect. Follicular lymphoma is usually CD10+.
Incorrect. Mantle cell lymphoma is CD5+.

claims.text: CLL phenotype and ≥ 5,000/µL ≥ 3 months; MBL definition; marrow cytopenia exception.
MCL phenotype and confirmation by cyclin D1/SOX11 or t(11;14).
FL CD10+ (~90%), CD5−, CD43−, BCL2 increased; t(14;18).
HCL markers, scatter, CD5−/CD10−, BRAF V600E 90–95%, TRAP IHC.
del17p as adverse marker; purine-analog therapy for HCL; Burkitt t(8;14)/starry sky; B-ALL TdT; FL bcl-6.
Reports invented; marker intensities described in words.

accuracyFlags.issue: Hit 8 gives ≥ 5 × 10⁹/L monoclonal B cells for CLL without the ≥ 3-month duration or the marrow-infiltrate cytopenia exception (Hallek 2025). Both are taught here.
Hit 10 lists BRAF V600E without a frequency; Shah 2026 reports it in 90–95% of classic HCL, so its absence does not exclude HCL.

morphology.note: No flow plots or cell images; phenotype cards are schematic.

verification.notes: 5 claims checked against Hallek 2025, Gajzer & Fromm 2025, Shah 2026 and Laganà 2025; 1 pending (prognosis, therapy, Burkitt/B-ALL, bcl-6). No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
